clue.text: Finished following fine trip

indicators.note: what follows a letter is everything after it, so only the part after the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to trip is to fall over
F is the pencil-grade and abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A trip that went well has just come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the part of FALL OVER that follows F: knock the fine off the trip and ALL OVER remains.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is all over it has ended completely, the same idea as being finished.

clue.text: Country road ran randomly

indicators.note: done at random means in no fixed order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country road that wanders about with no clear direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country road' reads as a rural lane, but 'Country' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small independent principality in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: Drop back to keep seat warm?

blocks.note: first meaning: fall behind the others
second, playful meaning: to lag is to insulate, and one's behind is one's seat

explanation.surface: Someone slips back a place in a queue just to keep their chair warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: to lag pipes is to wrap them against the cold, and a behind is the body's seat, so lagging your behind keeps it warm.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag behind is the idiom for trailing slower than others, which is dropping back.

clue.text: Upsetting part of sermon evoked rancour

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece inside it, so the letters lie within the words that follow
to upset something is to turn it over, so in a down clue the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A sermon so upsetting that parts of it stirred up bitterness in the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across serMON EVoked and read upwards to give VENOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in speech is spiteful bitterness, a close synonym for rancour or deep-seated ill will.

clue.text: Proper worker, a man indispensable to the boss

definitions.text: a man indispensable to the boss
definitions.note: the phrase defines the full expression right-hand man, of which the answer is the adjective

blocks.note: proper and right both mean correct or fitting
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A proper worker is the kind of employee a boss cannot do without.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the familiar phrase right-hand man, the boss's most trusted helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a chief assistant whom a leader relies on more than anyone else.

clue.text: Guide for riverside in Italy

blocks.note: the river half of this word: read with 'in Italy', it is the Po, Italy's longest river
with the side half of the word before: a side in Italy is Inter Milan, the football club

explanation.surface: A tour guide who shows visitors the riverside in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riverside' looks like one word to define, but it splits: the river, then a side, meaning a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a hint or indicator that steers someone in the right direction, which is a guide.

clue.text: Criticise extremely idiotic hysteria

indicators.note: the extremes of something are its two ends, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a bout of hysteria as utterly idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as an intensifier for 'idiotic', but it selects that word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden uncontrollable fear or anxiety, which is a form of hysteria.

clue.text: Popular oath can be impossible to say

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
eff is a euphemism for a well-known swear word
to be able is to be capable of doing, so can

explanation.surface: A favourite swear word can be too rude to utter.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a joke in the surface: the effing oath really is unsayable in polite company, which suits a word meaning too great to express.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffable describes something too great or extreme to be expressed in words.

clue.text: Conviction for injecting double energy into high explosive

indicators.note: to inject is to put something inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: TNT is the standard high explosive
E for energy, twice

explanation.surface: A criminal conviction for supercharging explosives with extra energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Es go into TNT separately, one after each of the first two letters, to give T-E-N-E-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief firmly held, which is a conviction in the sense of creed.

clue.text: Win support for essential truth from small part of England

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the middle letters are taken
in a down clue a support goes underneath, so one piece is written below the other

blocks.note: the three central letters of the word
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: Winning backing for a basic truth from a small corner of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Though 'Win' comes first in the clue, it supports the other piece, so it goes at the bottom. RUTLAND is the smallest historic county of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutland is England's smallest county, so it is literally a small part of the country.

clue.text: Become defensive when told to start eating  …

blocks.note: first meaning: entrench, like soldiers digging trenches
second meaning: the informal invitation to tuck into food

explanation.surface: Someone bristles when ordered to begin a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next one for surface flow only; each answer is solved alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is both to hold a fortified position stubbornly and the idiom urging diners to begin a meal.

clue.text: …  a biscuit red head produced

blocks.note: ginger is the colour of red hair
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A redhead brings out a biscuit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red head' looks like a person with red hair, but it is two words giving two pieces. A ginger nut is a hard British ginger-flavoured biscuit, a ginger snap.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger nut is a crisp spiced cookie, a standard variety of British biscuit.

clue.text: Irate chum suffering with stiff joints

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so its letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend is in a bad temper because their joints are stiff and painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering with stiff joints' reads as one phrase, but 'suffering' is the anagram signal and only the last three words define.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic describes someone affected by rheumatism, a condition causing painful, stiff joints and muscles.

clue.text: Authoritative ruling from soccer body that wants active leaders

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so each word gives only its first letter

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English soccer
the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A football association issues a ruling that it wants energetic captains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Active leaders' looks like a phrase about captains, but 'leaders' takes the initials of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a formal legal opinion issued by an Islamic scholar, an authoritative religious ruling.

clue.text: Cutting head of weed off when growing

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter is meant
something taken off is removed, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: the first letter
the moon waxes as it grows

explanation.surface: Snipping the top off a weed while it is still growing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the W from WAXING. The surface sounds like gardening, but 'Cutting' is the definition and 'head of weed' is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Axing means chopping with an axe, or cutting jobs and budgets, so it is a synonym of cutting.

clue.text: Division in band that's getting older

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a wing is a division of an army, party or building
a band of people or musicians is a group

explanation.surface: A split within a pop band whose members are ageing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division in band' reads like a rift between musicians; in fact the military or political sense of division gives a piece that sits inside the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing up is the process of maturing from child to adult, so it means getting older.

clue.text: Embittered expert judged to have stolen book

indicators.note: a thief who has stolen something holds it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: an ace is an expert
to rate something is to judge it
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A bitter specialist was found to have taken a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stolen' suggests a theft story, but it only signals that the book letter is held inside another piece. Acerbated is a rare word; exacerbated is its familiar cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbated means made bitter or harsh, an uncommon synonym of embittered.

clue.text: Alternative theatre is most indecent

indicators.note: an alternative is a different version, so the letters take another form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fringe theatre is the crudest kind of show around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative theatre' is a real genre, which hides that 'Alternative' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and bawdy, so the superlative earthiest means the crudest or most indecent.

clue.text: Dog at sea enabled Darwin to develop his evolutionary theory

definitions.text: Dog at sea enabled Darwin to develop his evolutionary theory

blocks.note: surface reading: a hound adrift on the ocean

blocks.clueFragment: enabled Darwin to develop his evolutionary theory
blocks.note: setter's reading: the survey ship, named after a dog breed, that carried Darwin to the Galapagos

explanation.surface: A dog at sea somehow helped Darwin arrive at evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog is a ship: HMS Beagle took Charles Darwin on the voyage whose observations led to his theory of natural selection.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Beagle was the naval survey vessel carrying Darwin around the world from 1831 to 1836.

clue.text: Dried rose cooked as an addition to main course

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef serves dried rose petals alongside the main dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' fits the food theme so neatly that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A side order is an extra dish such as fries or salad served alongside the principal meal.

clue.text: Player needing second income source when promise broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete forced into a second job after a contract promise falls through.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is long and descriptive: such a player is paid for sport but not enough to live on.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-professional plays for money but part-time, so also needs a regular day job to earn a living.

clue.text: Odds, oddly, may be this!

blocks.note: surface reading: a play on odd numbers, as if odds must be odd
setter's reading: betting odds of one to one carry the paradoxical name of their opposite

explanation.walkthrough: Betting odds are quoted as prices, and a one-to-one price has a name that sounds like the opposite of odd, hence 'oddly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, evens means odds of one to one, where a winning stake is doubled.

clue.text: Occasionally stern solicitor dispatched

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
a tout solicits custom, for instance selling tickets

explanation.surface: A lawyer who is sometimes severe has been sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it means anyone who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: To send something out is to dispatch it, as with letters or invitations.

clue.text: Nomads use trails central for these tribes people

indicators.note: what is central is in the middle, so only the middle letters count

blocks.note: the two central letters
the central letter
the two central letters

explanation.surface: Nomadic tribes follow paths that are central to their way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the middle of every word before 'central'. The Masai, also spelt Maasai, are semi-nomadic herders of Kenya and Tanzania.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are an East African people, traditionally cattle-herding tribesmen of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Small border plant

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a border is an edge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Border plant' reads as something for a flower border; 'border' is in the wordplay and 'plant' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Oxford museum compiled article on tree growth

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another follows it, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: the ash is a common tree
a mole is a growth on the skin
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An Oxford museum has put together a paper on how trees grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is placed after the other two pieces. The Ashmolean is Oxford University's museum of art and archaeology, Britain's oldest public museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean Museum in Oxford, founded in 1683, is the university's renowned collection of art and antiquities.

clue.text: Specialist language used to describe advance in painting?

indicators.note: something in another is enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: to go is to move forward
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: The jargon critics use to talk about a breakthrough in painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance in painting' sounds like an artistic breakthrough; 'advance' is simply the verb to move on, and 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang of a particular group, a specialised vocabulary used by insiders.

clue.text: Historical centre of holy study

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the inner letters are taken

blocks.note: the two central letters
a den is a small private room, a study

explanation.surface: Seminary studies once centred on holy matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of holy study' sounds like a seminary, but it splits into the middle of one word plus a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective meaning of a past era, as in olden days, so historical.

clue.text: Exercise expected to captivate eager teacher

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to take captive, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: PE is physical education
something due is expected
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: Workouts are supposed to enthuse a keen instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eager teacher' reads as one phrase, but 'eager' belongs to the wordplay and 'teacher' alone defines. PE is the school subject, physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster or instructor, often with a hint of pedantry, so a teacher.

clue.text: Pursue game that's hiding quietly

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Hunters stalk game animals that are lying low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like quarry for hunters, but it is the board game. Doggo is British slang, used in the phrase 'lie doggo', for keeping still and hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is informal British slang for staying motionless and out of sight, so hiding quietly.

clue.text: Abandoned pipe not mine

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone disowns a discarded pipe, insisting it isn't theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not mine' reads as a denial of ownership; 'mine' is the definition, the noun for a place where minerals are dug.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pit is a surface excavation for extracting coal or ore, a type of mine.

clue.text: Beat chap — it's not the main issue

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: Hitting a fellow is beside the point of the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing the thing rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a digression that strays from the central topic of a discussion.
